title: Marketplace Provisioning & Troubleshooting Guide (AWS + GCP)
author: Dev Patel
body:
## Purpose
This guide helps Customer Success (CS) and Support troubleshoot common issues experienced by customers who purchase Redwood Inference via AWS Marketplace or Google Cloud Marketplace.

Primary goals:
- Reduce time-to-activation for marketplace buyers.
- Standardize triage and escalation for entitlement and org-linking issues.
- Provide approved customer-facing templates for common scenarios.

## Audience
- Support engineers (L1/L2)
- Customer Success Managers
- Solutions Engineers supporting enterprise procurement

## High-level flow (what “good” looks like)
1) Customer purchases a Redwood offering in AWS/GCP Marketplace.
2) Marketplace sends entitlement/subscription events to Redwood.
3) Redwood creates/updates internal entitlements and exposes them to the Console.
4) Customer completes org linking in Redwood Console.
5) Customer can generate API keys / use Dedicated or Private onboarding path as per SKU.

If a buyer is “stuck,” it is almost always one of:
- Entitlement event not received or delayed.
- Entitlement received but not mapped to the intended Redwood org.
- Region mismatch between marketplace purchase and Redwood project/org configuration.
- Customer completed purchase but skipped org linking step.

## Definitions
- **Marketplace account**: AWS payer/account or GCP billing account that made the purchase.
- **Subscription/Entitlement**: The marketplace record representing the customer’s rights to use a SKU.
- **Redwood org**: Customer workspace in Redwood Console (billing + access boundaries).
- **Org linking**: Mapping the marketplace subscription to a specific Redwood org.
- **SKU**: Marketplace offer line item; maps to Redwood plan codes/entitlements.

## What to collect up front (required)
Ask for the following in the first response to reduce back-and-forth:

### AWS Marketplace
- AWS account ID that purchased (12-digit)
- AWS Marketplace product code / offer name (if visible)
- Date/time of purchase and AWS region (if shown)
- Customer email used to sign into Redwood Console

### GCP Marketplace
- GCP billing account ID (format: ######-######-######)
- Project ID associated with the purchase (if applicable)
- Date/time of purchase and chosen deployment region
- Customer email used to sign into Redwood Console

### Redwood
- Redwood org name + org slug (or org ID if they know it)
- Screenshot of the Console “Marketplace” section showing current status/error
- Whether they intended to link to an existing org vs a new org

## Internal tools / where to look
> Note: Access to internal admin tools is limited. If you do not have access, escalate using the paths below.

- **Console** (customer-facing): https://console.redwoodinference.com
- **Support admin (internal)**: https://admin.redwoodinference.com (org + entitlement inspection)
- **Logs/Tracing (internal)**: Observability dashboards under “Marketplace Onboarding”
  - Metrics commonly used: `marketplace_webhook_ingest_errors`, `marketplace_entitlement_lag_seconds`, `marketplace_org_link_failures`

Primary owning engineering teams:
- Entitlement mapping/control plane: **Ethan Park** (Eng)
- Billing/metering and plan codes: **Cole Summers** (Eng), **Nadia Rahman** (TL)
- SRE monitoring/escalations: **Rafael Mendes** (SRE)

## Severity and support targets (internal)
Use these to prioritize and set expectations.

- **SEV-1**: Customer has paid and cannot access any service; production impact; multiple users blocked; enterprise procurement deadline. Target: immediate escalation, updates every 60 minutes.
- **SEV-2**: Customer paid and is blocked for a specific org/region but workaround exists (e.g., link to correct org after reset). Target: escalation within 4 business hours.
- **SEV-3**: Confusion/education (how to link, where to find subscription ID), no hard block. Target: resolve within 2 business days.

## Quick triage decision tree
1) Confirm purchase completed in marketplace.
   - If NOT completed: direct customer to marketplace console and procurement/admin.
2) Is entitlement visible in Redwood Console?
   - If NO: likely webhook/entitlement ingestion delay.
   - If YES: proceed.
3) Is entitlement linked to the correct Redwood org?
   - If NO: wrong-org linking or multiple org confusion.
4) Does Console show a region mismatch error?
   - If YES: resolve region mismatch / routing policy.

## Common issues and fixes

### 1) Entitlement not showing up after purchase (delay / missing)
**Symptoms**
- Customer purchased 15–60+ minutes ago.
- Console shows “No marketplace entitlements found” or onboarding page loops.

**Likely causes**
- Marketplace event delay (AWS/GCP propagation).
- Webhook ingestion failure/retry backlog.
- Customer is signed into a different Redwood account than intended.

**Customer-facing steps (safe to suggest)**
1) Confirm the purchase shows as “Active” in AWS/GCP Marketplace.
2) Wait 15 minutes and refresh the Console.
3) Ensure they are signed into the correct Redwood email/SSO identity.
4) If still missing after 60 minutes, open a ticket with requested info (see “What to collect”).

**Internal steps**
1) Check the Marketplace Onboarding dashboard for elevated entitlement lag or ingest failures.
2) If errors correlate to AWS or GCP webhook endpoints, escalate to SRE (SEV-1 if paid and blocked).
3) If ingestion looks healthy globally, check if the entitlement exists but is not associated with the customer identity (requires admin tool access).

**Escalation**
- SEV-1 if customer is paid and fully blocked > 60 minutes.
- Route to: Control Plane Entitlements (Eng) + SRE.


### 2) Entitlement is present but linked to the wrong Redwood org
**Symptoms**
- Customer sees an active entitlement, but usage/keys are not available in the org they expected.
- Customer has multiple Redwood orgs (common for enterprises: sandbox + prod).

**Likely causes**
- User linked the subscription while logged into the wrong org.
- Customer used a different identity (personal email vs corporate SSO) during linking.
- Multiple marketplace accounts; the “payer” account differs from “builder” account.

**Customer-facing steps**
1) Ask them to confirm which org should own the subscription (org name + slug).
2) Ask them to navigate to Console → Settings → Marketplace and share a screenshot.
3) If they have access to the wrong org, ask them to switch orgs and check the Marketplace section.

**Internal remediation options**
- If policy allows: Unlink subscription from incorrect org and re-link to the correct org (admin action).
- If the customer cannot access the org that currently has the entitlement, coordinate with their org admins to add the correct user.

**Escalation**
- Route to: Console backend/org linking (Eng) + Control plane entitlements.


### 3) Region mismatch (GCP more common; also occurs on AWS)
**Symptoms**
- Console shows errors like “Region not supported for this subscription” or “Subscription purchased in region X cannot be provisioned in region Y.”
- Customer selected an EU region for procurement reasons but tries to deploy/use in a different region.

**Likely causes**
- Marketplace purchase is bound to a specific region/offer configuration.
- Redwood org default region differs from purchased region.
- Dedicated/Private SKU requires region capacity approval or provisioning lead time.

**Customer-facing resolution paths**
- If they can use the purchased region: instruct them to update Redwood org/project region selection to match.
- If they must use a different region for residency/compliance: they may need a different marketplace SKU/offer or a region-enabled entitlement.

**Internal steps**
1) Confirm purchased region in entitlement metadata (admin tools).
2) Confirm Redwood org routing/region configuration (regional policy owner: Mina Haddad).
3) If region capacity/provisioning is the blocker (Dedicated/Private), open an internal provisioning request and set timeline expectations.

**Escalation**
- Route to: Regional policy/routing owner + Dedicated/Private PM on-call channel (if applicable) + SRE if it’s a platform regression.


### 4) “Purchase succeeded, but I can’t generate an API key / start using Hosted API”
**Symptoms**
- Buyer expects immediate API usage but sees a linking wizard or “pending” status.

**Most common root cause**
- Org linking step not completed.

**Customer-facing steps**
1) Send the direct Console path: Console → Settings → Marketplace → “Link subscription.”
2) Verify they are in the correct org.
3) Once linked, have them navigate to Console → API Keys and create a key.

**If still blocked**
- Entitlement may be attached but plan not applied due to mapping error → escalate to Billing/Entitlements.


### 5) Duplicate purchases / multiple subscriptions
**Symptoms**
- Customer purchased twice (common when procurement tests).
- Confusion about which subscription is active.

**Customer-facing guidance**
- We can generally link one active subscription per intended org, depending on SKU type.
- If they accidentally purchased multiple times, they should coordinate cancellation/refund via the marketplace per marketplace policy.

**Internal steps**
- Determine which subscription is active and which is intended.
- Do not promise refunds; defer to marketplace policy and Finance/Legal.

**Escalation**
- Route to Finance/Legal sponsor if customer requests billing/legal commitments.


### 6) Dedicated/Private SKU provisioning questions (“What happens after purchase?”)
**Symptoms**
- Customer expects dedicated capacity to appear instantly.

**Correct expectation**
- Hosted API access is typically immediate after linking.
- Dedicated and Private provisioning may require coordination (capacity assignment, VPC details, allowlists, KMS choices).

**Customer-facing steps**
1) Confirm SKU purchased (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
2) If Dedicated/Private: collect required deployment info and schedule an onboarding call.
3) Provide a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) style checklist (see template below).

**Escalation**
- Route to Solutions Engineering (Markus Klein’s team) + provisioning owner.

## Standard internal escalation paths
When escalating, include:
- Marketplace (AWS/GCP), time of purchase, region
- Customer org slug, customer email/identity
- Screenshot of Console error
- Severity and business impact (paid + blocked, deadline)

### If ingestion/webhook failures are suspected
- Page: SRE on-call
- Include: dashboard links + timestamps

### If mapping/plan code appears incorrect
- Route: Billing/Metering (Cole Summers) + Control Plane Entitlements (Ethan Park)

### If org linking UI is broken or confusing
- Route: Console backend lead (Chloe Martin)

### If customer asks security/compliance evidence questions while blocked
- Route: Security & Compliance (Marcus Lin / Olga Petrov) via internal intake

## Customer-facing templates (approved macros)

### Template A: Acknowledge purchase; entitlement still processing
Subject: Redwood Marketplace purchase received — entitlement activation in progress

Hi {{CustomerName}},

Thanks for purchasing Redwood Inference via {{AWS Marketplace|Google Cloud Marketplace}}. In most cases, entitlements appear in the Redwood Console within a few minutes, but it can occasionally take up to ~60 minutes.

In the meantime, could you confirm the following so we can verify the subscription on our side?
- Marketplace: {{AWS account ID | GCP billing account ID}}
- Purchase time (approx) + region
- Redwood org name/slug you want to link
- The email you’re using to sign into the Redwood Console

If the entitlement still isn’t visible after 60 minutes, reply to this thread and we’ll escalate immediately.

Best regards,
{{AgentName}}
Redwood Support


### Template B: Wrong org linked (needs re-link)
Subject: Marketplace subscription linked to the wrong Redwood org — next steps

Hi {{CustomerName}},

It looks like the marketplace subscription is currently linked to a different Redwood org than the one you intended.

To resolve this quickly, please confirm:
1) The Redwood org name/slug that should own the subscription
2) Whether you have access to the org where the subscription currently appears (Console → Settings → Marketplace)

Once confirmed, we can help you re-link the subscription to the correct org.

Best regards,
{{AgentName}}
Redwood Support


### Template C: Region mismatch explanation + options
Subject: Marketplace region mismatch — how to proceed

Hi {{CustomerName}},

Thanks for the details. Your marketplace purchase is associated with region {{PurchasedRegion}}, but the Redwood org/project is currently configured for {{CurrentRegion}}. Marketplace subscriptions can be region-scoped depending on the listing and offer configuration.

Options:
1) Update the Redwood org/project to use {{PurchasedRegion}} (fastest if acceptable for your requirements), or
2) If you must use {{RequiredRegion}} for residency/compliance, we can review the appropriate marketplace offer/SKU and next steps with you.

Reply with your preferred region requirement and we’ll guide you to the quickest path.

Best regards,
{{AgentName}}
Redwood Support


### Template D: Dedicated/Private post-purchase onboarding checklist (MAP-lite)
Subject: Next steps for Redwood Dedicated/Private via Marketplace

Hi {{CustomerName}},

Great — we see your marketplace purchase. For Dedicated/Private deployments, there are a few setup items needed before we can provision capacity and complete onboarding.

Please share:
- Target cloud + region(s)
- Expected traffic profile (TPS, peak concurrency, model(s), sequence lengths)
- Networking requirements (VPC/VNet, private connectivity, allowlists)
- Identity requirements (SSO/SAML, SCIM if applicable)
- Key management requirements (KMS/HSM preferences)
- Target go-live date and environments (dev/stage/prod)

We can schedule an onboarding call with Solutions Engineering to confirm requirements and timeline.

Best regards,
{{AgentName}}
Redwood Support

## Notes on what we should NOT promise
- Do not promise refunds, credits, or cancellation outcomes for marketplace purchases. Direct to marketplace policy and involve Finance/Legal.
- Do not claim certifications (SOC 2 / ISO) beyond what is currently approved in the Security FAQ. If the customer requests evidence, follow the approved process.
- Do not promise data residency guarantees outside documented regions/controls.

## Runbook checklist (internal)
Use this checklist before escalating:
- [ ] Confirm purchase is “Active” in AWS/GCP marketplace (customer-provided screenshot or confirmation).
- [ ] Confirm customer identity and intended Redwood org.
- [ ] Check Console for entitlement status and any explicit error.
- [ ] Check Marketplace Onboarding dashboard for systemic issues.
- [ ] If user error (org linking), send the correct Console path and template.
- [ ] If platform issue suspected, escalate with complete context.
